Question: Square \(ABCD\) has side length \(1.\) Points \(P,\) \(Q,\) \(R,\) and \(S\) each lie on a side of \(ABCD\) such that \(APQCRS\) is an equilateral convex hexagon with side length \(s.\) What is \(s?\)
Solution:
Look at the corner of the square cut off by side \(PQ\) of the hexagon. Label the square as in the figure, with \(P\) on \(AB\) and \(Q\) on \(BC\).

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_10A_Q05_official_solution_fig1.png)

All hexagon sides equal \(s\), so \(AP=QC=PQ=s\). Since each square side has length \(1\), we have \(BP=BQ=1-s\). Triangle \(BPQ\) is right-angled at \(B\), and the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
PQ=\sqrt{(1-s)^2+(1-s)^2}=\sqrt2(1-s).
\]
But \(PQ=s\), so
\[
s=\sqrt2(1-s),\qquad
s=\frac{\sqrt2}{1+\sqrt2}=\boxed{2-\sqrt2}.
\]
The answer is C. The useful move is to express the small right triangle's legs as the full square side minus a known hexagon side.
